analysis.title: Longevity weekly pulse #83: Key takeaways from health care conference season
key_insights: UBS CIO sees incrementally positive signals from health care conferences, with structural demand and innovation supportive across cardiometabolic disease, oncology and immunology, plus potential AI productivity upside.

With health care valuations above historical levels, UBS expects future returns to depend more on pipeline quality, execution and conversion of innovation into durable earnings growth, so stock selection matters more.

Pharma managements stressed portfolio diversification and pipeline execution to handle upcoming patent expirations (LoEs). BD remains a lever but some large caps have less immediate need after internal pipeline wins.
Obesity remains a key innovation area. Differentiation is expected from efficacy, convenience and persistence, with oral, longer-acting and combination approaches broadening the treated population.
Oncology stays innovation-rich, with ADCs, bispecific antibodies and personalized cancer vaccines the focus areas.
AI is becoming a productivity enabler but monetization will be gradual. The Pfizer CEO said it moves from efficiency to growth, with cost lines benefiting first and sales last.
UBS thinks companies with proprietary data, broad technology platforms and the ability to embed AI in workflows are best placed to capture AI benefits.
China is both an innovation source (faster timelines, lower development costs, more licensing deals) and a competitive and pricing threat, especially in established pharma products and diagnostics.
AstraZeneca cited up to USD 20bn of potential pipeline readouts in 2027 and limited major LoEs beyond 2030. Large-scale BD is not seen as necessary.
Roche expects a record five launches in 2027. Giredestrant (USD 3-5bn peak sales potential) and fenebrutinib are near-term drivers, with Ocrevus LoE through 2030 a headwind.
Galderma cited China as its second-largest market and Nemluvio at about USD 1bn in sales. It reiterated a 26% EBITDA margin ambition for this year.

Effective 1 November 2026 UBS CIO no longer rates equities as Most Preferred or Least Preferred and instead uses a CIO Selected designation. Amgen and Gilead were added as CIO Selected to the Longevity list on Nov 11 2026.

market_movers.rationale: Management confident on medium-term growth, up to USD 20bn of potential pipeline readouts in 2027 and limited major LoEs beyond 2030.
Record five launches expected in 2027, with giredestrant at USD 3-5bn peak sales potential and fenebrutinib as key drivers.
Galderma has no US listing. Growth drivers are international expansion, injectables and prescription dermatology, with Nemluvio near USD 1bn in sales and a 26% EBITDA margin ambition.
Added as CIO Selected to the Longevity list on Nov 11 2026.

sector_views.rationale: Constructive long-term view on aging demographics and innovation, but valuations above historical levels make stock selection more important.

earnings_insights: No earnings prints in this note. Management commentary only: AstraZeneca guided to up to USD 20bn of potential pipeline readouts in 2027 (company framing, not a financial estimate).
Galderma reiterated a 26% EBITDA margin ambition for this year, a company target.
risk_factors: Pipeline failures and patent expirations (LoEs) across large-cap pharma.
Drug pricing pressure, including in China for established products and diagnostics.
Valuations above historical levels leave less room for execution misses.
AstraZeneca China slowdown (13% of revenues) from government investigations, and US IRA and Part D redesign impact.
Novo Nordisk reliance on GLP-1 volumes and pricing, and adverse CagriSema data.
Galderma Nemluvio launch slowed by US payer hurdles.
geopolitical: China is increasingly shaping the global biopharma sector as both an innovation source and a pricing and competitive pressure.
